text:
Aisha (PM): Heads-up: execs want a short memo + acceptance test checklist for enterprise evidence exports. Goal: one-click export ZIP for customers that proves chain-of-custody + retention headers. Need owners and a clear minimal spec by EOD Friday.
Noah (CS): Customers keep asking for a verified export they can hand to auditors. Must include logs, manifest, and signatures. Ideally a verify.sh they can run.
Ravi (Security): Security checklist: (1) logs written to append-only store with immutable IDs, (2) per-batch signatures (HMAC or sigv4), (3) manifest with keyIDs + rotation history, (4) tamper-evidence path (Merkle root or batch HMACs).
Liam (Eng-Platform): Implementation question: do we bundle customer's BYOK-encrypted keys inside export or just metadata + KMS audit logs? Security risk either way. Prefer metadata + KMS audit lines and a proof-of-encryption field.
Jo (Legal): We cannot export customer key material. Exports may include key IDs and attestation statements, plus an exported audit log of KMS access events. Also need to log who requested the export (user + approvals).
Marta (SRE): Runbook note: export generation must be queued to a dedicated worker pool to avoid noisy spikes. Add rate-limits and a backpressure signal to the console. If worker pool is saturated, surface ETA and option for staggered delivery.
Zoe (Eng-ML): Add small perf note: evidence exports for long chat sessions can be huge (tokens). We should offer two flavors: full-fidelity and summarized (with pointers to raw blobs in WORM store). Customer chooses.
Liam (Eng-Platform): Draft manifest example (YAML snippet):
```
manifest_version: 1
tenant: tenant-987
exported_at: 2026-03-20T14:05:00Z
exported_by: alice@example.com
items:
  - path: logs/2026-03-20/part-0001.gz
    type: audit-log
    hmac: sha256:deadbeef...
  - path: sessions/longsession-42.tar.gz
    type: session-record
    encryption: kms:cust-key-123
signature: sigv4:abc123...
```
Ravi (Security): Also require a signed manifest manifest.hmac per export and an accompanying verify script that validates each hmac and signature. Put sample verify CLI in the ZIP.
Noah (CS): Acceptance test idea: create tenant test-export -> trigger export via UI/API -> receive ZIP -> run verify.sh -> validate manifest hashes match and signature verifies -> confirm retention headers present. This should be in the customer acceptance suite.
Aisha (PM): Ownership: Eng-Platform -> manifest + worker queue + routing; Security -> hmac/signature formats + verify scripts; SRE -> worker pool/backpressure/runbook; CS -> acceptance tests; Legal -> export approval metadata + retention labels. Target sign-off: next Friday product review.
Jo (Legal): Also capture escape-hatch policy: if an export contains data subject to a legal hold, the export must be blocked and an approval workflow kicked off (2x Legal + 1x Compliance). Record timestamps and approvers in the audit trail.
Marta (SRE): Simulation: I'll run two drills next Wed: (A) worker-saturation path -> delayed exports and ETA path, (B) export blocked due to legal hold -> approval flow and blocked notification. Invite CS & Legal.
Liam (Eng-Platform): Routing policy for export generation (pseudo):
```
export_policy:
  - condition: worker_pool_free >= 2
    action: start_immediately
  - condition: worker_pool_free == 0
    action: queue_with_eta
  - condition: legal_hold=true
    action: block_and_notify
```
Aisha (PM): Can someone draft a 1-page PRD with the manifest schema, export flow, and acceptance test steps? I'll include estimated level-of-effort.
Ravi (Security): I'll drop a short spec for HMAC vs sig choices and provide a recommended CLI for verification.
export-bot: Export-worker queued job 77321 for tenant-987 at 2026-03-18T09:41:03Z
Noah (CS): Thanks — I'll map customer test scenarios and email stakeholders the list.
Aisha (PM): Great work. Keep it terse; execs want the memo + checklist. :eyes:
